open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which authority supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at`?
options: an injected UTC system clock
an ambient system-clock call in the mark operation
an instant supplied by the caller
open_points.default_guess: Inject a UTC system clock into the mark operation and read it while holding the project lock.

witness.initial: A placement exists and has no publication mark.
events: The caller asks the service to record a Portal `photo_id`.
The deliverer creates the publication mark.
outcomes: The deliverer obtains `marked_at` from an injected system clock.
The deliverer accepts a caller-provided instant or reads an ambient clock directly.
witness.observer: A reader of the stored publication mark sees a different timestamp and different trust boundary.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.text: The calling flow reports the `photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: At which event is `marked_at` sampled, and how many clock readings may one mark operation take—on request receipt, before waiting for the project lock, after taking the lock, immediately before writing, or after the rename?
options: one reading after validation and lock acquisition, immediately before constructing the mark
one reading when the request arrives
multiple readings with one selected for the stored value
open_points.default_guess: Take exactly one reading inside the project lock after all refusal checks and immediately before constructing the mark.

witness.initial: Another process holds the project lock for several minutes while no mark exists.
events: A caller submits a valid mark request.
The request waits for the project lock.
The lock becomes available and the mark is written.
outcomes: `marked_at` records the time the request arrived.
`marked_at` records the later time at which the mark was committed.
witness.observer: The caller and every later scan or record reader can see timestamps separated by the lock wait.

open_points.subject: datetime representation
open_points.question: What exact representation must every written or compared instant use, including timezone awareness, UTC normalization, JSON spelling, fractional-second precision and comparison precision?
options: timezone-aware UTC datetimes serialized with `Z`
naive datetimes whose values are defined to be UTC, serialized without an offset
UTC datetimes serialized with an explicit `+00:00` offset
open_points.default_guess: Use timezone-aware UTC internally, serialize with `Z` at microsecond precision, and compare normalized UTC instants.

witness.initial: A mark is created at a UTC instant having non-zero microseconds.
events: The deliverer serializes the mark record.
A later operation reads and validates the record.
outcomes: The record contains an aware value such as `2026-11-19T10:00:00.123456Z` and preserves its precision.
The record contains a naive or rounded value such as `2026-11-19T10:00:00`.
witness.observer: Record readers and equality tests see different `marked_at` values.

open_points.subject: M03 PreparedPhoto.taken_at
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: When a camera record contains a local date and time but no UTC offset, how is it converted to the required UTC instant?
options: treat the camera value as already UTC
interpret it in a configured camera or deployment timezone
use an EXIF offset when present and otherwise fall back to file modification time
preserve the wall-clock fields while merely omitting an offset
open_points.default_guess: Use a camera-record offset when present; if no offset makes the camera value an instant, fall back to the file modification time.

witness.initial: A source JPEG has EXIF date `2026-07-01 12:00:00` with no offset and a modification time corresponding to `10:00:00Z`.
events: The caller delivers the JPEG.
The service prepares M03 and builds M05.
outcomes: `photo_date` is `12:00:00` UTC because the EXIF fields are treated as UTC.
`photo_date` is `10:00:00` UTC because the EXIF fields are interpreted in Europe/Madrid or the modification time is used.
witness.observer: The Portal and owner see a two-hour difference in the photo date.

open_points.subject: A6 folder creation
open_points.text: a folder it finds is accepted, whoever created it, also a concurrent call, when it is a folder; a missing one is created with the mode of the imported `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the binary store and of the imported `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the state folder, set whatever the process umask. In the state folder an entry on the way that is a symbolic link or not a folder fails the write, and a failure to create a folder or set its mode fails it too
open_points.question: If a folder is absent when checked but a concurrent call creates it before this call's creation attempt, must the losing call re-check and accept the folder, or must its failed exclusive creation fail the write?
options: treat an already-exists result as a race, re-open without following links, and accept it if it is a folder
treat every failed creation call, including already-exists, as a failed write
open_points.default_guess: Re-check after an already-exists result and accept only an actual folder; fail for every other creation error.

witness.initial: The state root exists but `locks` does not.
events: Process A and process B both check for `locks` and find it absent.
Process A creates `locks` with the required mode.
Process B attempts to create `locks` and receives an already-exists error.
outcomes: Process B re-checks the entry, accepts Process A's folder and continues to the project lock.
Process B treats its creation failure as `STATE_UNAVAILABLE` and refuses the operation.
witness.observer: Process B's caller sees success or a refusal for the same concurrent history.

open_points.subject: A6 state-folder traversal
open_points.text: In the state folder an entry on the way that is a symbolic link or not a folder fails the write
open_points.question: What must happen if an entry changes between being checked and being used, and must traversal and creation be anchored to already-open parent directories so that a symbolic-link substitution cannot redirect the operation?
options: open every segment relative to an already-open parent with no-follow semantics and fail on any substitution
perform path-based checks followed by ordinary path-based creation or opening
assume no actor can change state-folder entries and state that assumption explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Anchor each step to an open parent directory, use no-follow semantics, and fail the operation if the entry changes or cannot be verified.

witness.initial: The state root exists and an actor able to modify it can replace `ledger` during a delivery.
events: The deliverer checks that `ledger` is a folder.
The actor replaces `ledger` with a symbolic link.
The deliverer creates or renames the placement record using the textual path.
outcomes: The anchored traversal detects the replacement and refuses the write.
The path-based implementation follows the new link and writes outside the intended state folder.
witness.observer: The caller sees refusal versus success, and the filesystem owner sees the record at a different location.

open_points.subject: A6 lock file
open_points.text: Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none. Atomicity is per file.
open_points.question: Does “Each file” include the lock file, or are lock files created and opened directly under rule 4 without the temporary-write, rename and folder-synchronisation protocol?
options: the protocol applies only to stored images and placement or mark records
the protocol applies to the lock file as well
the lock file uses a separately specified exclusive-create protocol
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the lock file from rule 3 and create/open it directly with no-follow and exact-mode handling under rule 4.

witness.initial: The project has no lock file.
events: Two processes attempt the project's first operation concurrently.
Each process needs to create and lock the lock file.
outcomes: Both use one stable lock-file inode created directly, so the operating-system lock serializes them.
Each follows the temporary-file and rename wording, allowing the processes to open or lock different inodes before or across replacement.
witness.observer: The callers can observe serialized operations or two operations entering the protected section concurrently.

open_points.subject: A6 temporary-file cleanup
open_points.text: A write that fails before the rename leaves the destination as it was, whether absent or holding an earlier complete file, and removes its temporary file.
open_points.question: If removing the temporary file also fails, what result is returned, which error controls the result, and may the temporary entry remain?
options: return the original write failure and allow the unremovable temporary entry to remain
replace the original failure with a cleanup failure
retry cleanup until it succeeds
treat failure to remove the temporary file as an invariant breach with a specified refusal
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the original operation failure, make a bounded best-effort cleanup attempt, and permit the temporary entry to remain unread and ignored if cleanup fails.

witness.initial: A destination folder permits creating and writing a temporary file but removal later fails.
events: The service creates the temporary file.
A pre-rename synchronisation or mode-setting operation fails.
The service attempts and fails to remove the temporary file.
outcomes: The operation reports the original mapped failure and leaves an ignored temporary file.
The cleanup error changes the reported failure or the operation keeps retrying and does not return.
witness.observer: The caller sees a different result or delay, and the filesystem owner sees whether the temporary file remains.

open_points.subject: INV-12 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-12: concurrent placements of one source answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed`, and marks from separate processes with two `photo_id` values answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
open_points.question: Must the placement test also run placements in separate processes and explicitly show that only one placement record and one stored image exist, as required by the across-process rule and the invariant that two placements are never produced?
options: require a separate-process placement race and inspect the resulting durable files as well as responses
treat concurrent in-process calls and response statuses alone as sufficient
split the invariant into in-process placement and cross-process mark guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Require separate-process races for both placements and marks, assert the response partition, and inspect that exactly one valid placement record, stored image and mark remain.

witness.initial: No placement or mark exists for a source.
events: Two independent service processes deliver the source concurrently.
Both return responses, after which the state and binary stores are inspected.
outcomes: A test checks only responses from same-process concurrency and therefore does not exercise the operating-system lock across processes.
A test races separate processes and proves both the responses and the single durable placement.
witness.observer: The test suite can pass an implementation whose lock works between threads but not between processes.
